stem: The monthly salaries (in Rs) of five employees in a firm are: 18000, 24000, 31000, 27000, 21000. If each employee receives an increment of Rs 3000, the range of the new salary distribution is:

per_option_rationale.rationale: Range is invariant under a shift (adding the same constant to each value). Original range = 31000 - 18000 = 13000. After increment, range remains 13000.
Student adds the increment to the original range: 13000 + 3000 = 16000, incorrectly believing a shift changes the range.
Student subtracts the increment from the original range: 13000 - 3000 = 10000.
Student adds the increment twice (once to each extreme): 13000 + 3000 + 3000 = 19000, as if both endpoints shift by 3000 in opposite directions.

explanation: When a constant is added to every observation, the maximum and minimum each increase by the same amount. So the difference (range) stays unchanged at 31000 - 18000 = 13000.

explanation_sections.punchline: Range is invariant under a change of origin; adding a constant to all values does not change the range.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify property: range = Max - Min. After adding constant c to all values, new range = (Max + c) - (Min + c) = Max - Min = original range. Compute: 31000 - 18000 = 13000.
explanation_sections.lesson: Measures of dispersion that use differences (range, mean deviation, standard deviation) are unaffected by adding a constant to all data points.
explanation_sections.timing: 30 seconds. Recognise invariance immediately; compute original range once. Trap: adding 3000 to the range.
